reasons: Documented OHTTP relay implementation with strict header allow-list behavior.
Independent third-party relay model matches RFC 9458 trust separation.
NCC Group publicly documented Fastly acting as Oblivious Relay in Meta/WhatsApp private processing.
must_reconfirm: Current commercial availability in 2026 for a small/new privacy service.
RFC 9458 production compatibility and supported OHTTP media types.
Ability to map only to the nominated La Bête gateway.
Header stripping policy and absence of identifying relay-to-gateway headers.
Request/IP logging, retention, operator access and customer-access controls.
Service-level metrics only or equivalent privacy-preserving observability.

reasons: Current managed OHTTP Relay documentation explicitly states RFC/IETF OHTTP support.
Global managed relay service designed to hide client IP from the application backend.
constraints: Current public documentation states Enterprise-only and closed beta/select privacy-oriented partners.
Access and commercial eligibility must be confirmed before selection.

disqualifiers: Relay operated by the same legal/operational entity as the gateway.
Relay forwards client IP, Forwarded, Via, User-Agent, Cookie, Authorization or stable pseudonymous identifiers to gateway.
Raw request logs are accessible to the gateway operator.

evidence_required: Separate operator credentials and access control from relay provider.
Public TLS endpoint with certificate lifecycle evidence.
RFC 9458 gateway configuration and HPKE key rotation evidence.
No client IP available at gateway.
Batching input accepts only opaque/validated OHTTP-decapsulated ballot payloads.

reasons: PKCS#11 Client SDK 5 supports RSA 2048-4096.
PKCS#11 mechanism set includes CKM_RSA_X_509 sign/verify, needed for the raw RSA private operation over the already encoded/blinded representative.
CloudHSM supports non-extractable keys when explicitly configured; production must not use extractable defaults.
proof_requirements: RSA-2048 key generated inside HSM, not generated in software then imported.
CKA_EXTRACTABLE=false and inability to transition to extractable.
CKA_SIGN=true; disable decrypt/wrap/unwrap/encrypt where technically possible for issuer key.
Successful blind-RSA interoperability test through PKCS#11 without exporting private material.
Separate Crypto Officer / Crypto User administration and documented dual-control procedure.
Rotation drill with overlap window and old-key verification.
Tamper-evident or immutable key-usage audit logs.

reasons: Current nShield PKCS#11 documentation includes CKM_RSA_X_509 and RSA 2048+.
Supports non-extractable/private-key controls and hardware-backed lifecycle management.

disqualifiers: Private key exportable or software-generated production key.
No raw RSA/CKM_RSA_X_509 equivalent required by blind signing flow.
Single administrator can create, export, rotate and destroy production issuer key without independent approval.

reasons: Publicly documented reviews of privacy-preserving systems involving IP-blinding relays, HSMs, key directories and cryptographic protocols.
Public Google Private AI Compute review included security analysis of an IP-blinding relay.
Public Meta/WhatsApp work documents Fastly as an Oblivious Relay in a privacy-sensitive production architecture.
scope_required: RFC 9474 / RFC 9578 Blind RSA design and CIRCL runtime integration.
RFC 9458 OHTTP + RFC 9292 BHTTP client/relay/gateway implementation.
Header minimization, traffic-analysis assumptions, HPKE key/context handling.
Persistent batching, anonymity-set policy and timing leakage.
HSM/PKCS#11 raw-RSA integration and key ceremony.
Collusion analysis across membership authority, issuer, relay, gateway, batcher and registry.

reasons: Recent public assessments cover cryptography, key management, TEE/privacy architecture and infrastructure.
Separate reviewer reduces single-auditor blind spots.
scope_required: Adversarial privacy threat model independent of NCC findings.
Relay/gateway deployment review and logging/observability checks.
HSM administration and operational separation review.
Public-vs-private data boundary and failure-mode review.

reasons: Dedicated cryptography practice covering protocols, primitives and implementations.
Recent public HSM provisioning and cryptography reviews.
Offers design assessment, implementation review, fuzzing/tooling and retest.
Regional network explicitly accompanies Scop and Scic creation and development.
Can review statutes, colleges, admission process and governance before any legally binding vote.

sequencing: RFI relay in parallel to Fastly and Cloudflare.
Technical validation session with AWS CloudHSM; nShield as fallback if raw-RSA/key-control requirements cannot be met.
RFP to NCC Group using the frozen audit pack and source commit.
Independent privacy review RFP to Cure53; Trail of Bits held as fallback/second opinion.
Parallel SCIC governance session with URSCOP Hauts-de-France.
No production activation until relay contract, HSM evidence, approved anonymity policy, external crypto audit, privacy review and SCIC legal gates all pass.
